output.brief: The fall in incidents is not real. Platform records show Corvane still reached about 36–37 confirmed incidents a month in September and October, the same as before the migration. Of those, 47 were moved to "Suspicious Activity–Monitoring" by a script. The script ran from a Brackwater analyst jump host using the integration account. It watched for confirmed cases about to breach the 4-hour containment limit, then changed their category 1–12 minutes after they appeared. This was deliberate, not a connector fault. It removes those cases from the incident count and from the containment and SLA figures. That is why Brackwater reports 100% SLA compliance and the bonus looks triggered. The growing monitoring queue (40 to 96) fits this. Do not approve the retainer cut or the bonus. Reinstate the 47 cases as incidents, have your in-house team and Halvard check whether each was actually contained, and remove category-edit rights from the Brackwater integration role. Then ask Brackwater for a written explanation before renewal. Hold off on invoicing service credits until the contract terms and the facts are confirmed. I have not checked whether the 28 dropped detection rules are missing attacks. Do that review separately. I'm about 85–90% sure of the main conclusion.
